A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same human-annotated complementary-label benchmark study, expanded and renamed CLImage in v3. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original human-annotation statistics, classifier benchmark results and experiments investigating noise, bias, validation and overfitting.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports additional TinyImageNet-derived benchmarks, annotation-consistency analyses and AutoAugment results.

M1.justification: The collection procedure still presents four sampled labels to each of three annotators. The CLL algorithms and transition-matrix interpolation procedure are retained. The explicit protocol steps and Appendix D explain existing procedures rather than introduce a new learning method.

E1.justification: v3 adds CLMicroImageNet10 and CLMicroImageNet20, representing distinct TinyImageNet-derived image classes, alongside their uniformly generated complementary-label counterparts. These datasets extend both standard and validation benchmarks beyond v2's CIFAR-derived coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ordinary-supervision references and evaluates FWD-R and URE-GA-R on uniform datasets where v2 reported dashes. The validation comparison also adds ROB-MAE. ROB-MAE corresponds to the existing MAE baseline; its renaming alone is not an algorithm addition.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes reported label selection from a random collected label to the first collected label. The main benchmark now reports early-stopped models instead of both final-epoch and early-stopped models. Appendix H adds an AutoAugment condition; the principal architecture, optimizer, training budget and validation split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices G and H add annotation-trial consistency analysis and an AutoAugment sensitivity experiment. Conversely, v3 removes the URE-GA, L-W/L-UW and PC-sigmoid noise-cleaning curves from v2's Appendix C, retaining FWD and SCL in Appendix E. Existing multiple-label, synthetic-noise, augmentation-removal and matrix-interpolation analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2's validation table reports point estimates, whereas v3's Tables 3–4 add ± uncertainty values. Appendix G newly reports noise rates separately for three collection trials. Standard benchmarks retain four-seed reporting; the PDFs do not establish an increase in run counts.

E6.justification: Common benchmark scores are replaced under revised settings: CLCIFAR10 FWD-U accuracy is 36.83±1.17 with early stopping in v2 and 34.83±0.50 in v3. These are not a same-setting performance comparison. v3 also adds MicroImageNet benchmark and validation results, annotation noise rates of 5.19% and 3.21%, trial statistics and AutoAugment scores.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds explicit mathematical loss definitions for existing baselines, including SCL-NL/SCL-EXP and discriminative modeling. The original CLL assumptions, validation estimators and transition-matrix interpolation remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central dataset contribution expands from two CIFAR-derived datasets to the four-dataset CLImage collection. The abstract, introduction and conclusion also identify complementary-label-only validation as a central practical barrier and call for improved validation schemes alongside the retained noise and bias claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A qualifies dataset generality and distinguishes assumption analysis from efficient label collection. v3 reframes CIFAR10 annotation preferences from label-name length to vehicle/animal categories and explicitly interprets ordinary-label validation as potentially optimistic. It removes v2's caveat about comparing annotation noise across different collection protocols.

D1.justification: Appendices B.5 and F document TinyImageNet class folders, label mappings and 500 training/50 validation images per class. v3 clarifies empirical transition-matrix computation, updates hardware and repository information, and reports AutoAugment's approximately doubled runtime. The earlier disclosure about superclass reference images is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 positions CLImage as an extension of the 2023 CLCIFAR release, cites subsequent studies using it and claims the first TinyImageNet-derived CLL datasets. It adds supporting dataset, architecture, augmentation and loss-correction references while dropping the multiple-complementary-label citation to Feng et al. The central research gap remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and authorship change, and the introduction, algorithm overview and dataset motivations are substantially rewritten. Validation becomes a standalone Section 6. The appendices are reorganized and expanded with limitations, algorithm explanations and collection/augmentation discussions, producing substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned around eight dataset conditions and an ordinary-supervision reference, dropping final-epoch columns. Validation is split across Tables 3–4. Distribution and transition-matrix figures are redrawn and regrouped, 20-class panels move to the appendix, and new trial, augmentation and class-mapping displays accompany the removed cleaning panels.

improvement.justification: TinyImageNet coverage, supervised references, validation uncertainty and clearer construction details make v3 a more useful benchmark. These gains are partly offset by removed noise-cleaning evidence and incomplete integration of appendix results. For example, Table 11's 6.69-point FWD-U CLCIFAR10 early-stopping gain uses v2's 36.83 baseline, whereas v3's Table 1 reports 34.83. The additions support a net improvement, but these reporting issues limit its magnitude.
